content.text:
The edit path already exists — it's in the Inspector, in a "Grid" section that appears when you select a module.

How it works:

- **Select a module on the canvas**, and the Inspector (right panel) shows a **Grid** section: an 8×5 replica of the module's device page, with every module on that page shown in its live slot (this module at full color, neighbors dimmed).
- **Click any button in that mini-grid** — the module moves there and gets **pinned** (a pin icon appears). The rest of the page reflows around it automatically.
- **Unpin** (the link button next to the pin icon) hands the slot back to automatic flow placement.

The underlying model, for context:

- Auto-assignment is `reflowGrid()` in `Sources/ZoiaCanvas/Model/PatchDocument.swift:404` — unpinned modules get packed first-fit in signal-flow order after every structural change. Pinned modules never move during reflow, so a manual placement sticks.
- The click-to-pin UI is `gridSection` / `gridButtons` in `Sources/ZoiaCanvas/Views/InspectorView.swift:69-131`.
- If pinning pushes a page over 40 buttons, the section shows a red "Page over 40 buttons — export is blocked" warning and export refuses with a per-page reason.

One caveat flagged in the code itself: button span is assumed to be one button per active block, marked as unverified against real hardware — worth checking against the pedal on a multi-block module before trusting a tight layout.

The minimap on the canvas is display-only; all editing goes through the Inspector's grid. If you'd rather drag modules directly on the minimap, that would be new work — say the word and I'll add it.

What's missing is the ability to drag to the grid location I want. I also don't like the idea of pinning it. If it's been placed somewhere, either manually or automatically, it doesn't get moved around. The exception is that if you drag something into a place that overlaps it, it moves out of the way (and returns to its spot if you move your placement elsewhere). Similarly, if an object next to it has additional parameters enabled (and thus more LEDs on the grid), it should move out of the way to accommodate that. I also noticed that if I highlight an element and use the Cmd+Del keyboard shortcut, the inspector on the right goes away, but the module itself stays. It won't delete unless I right-click and delete.

Three changes, then: drag-to-place on the inspector grid, replace pinning with sticky placement plus displacement, and the Cmd+Del bug. Let me read the relevant code first — starting with the Cmd+Del path since that's a straight bug.

All three changes are in and the full suite passes (223 tests, 8 of them the rewritten grid suite). Nothing is committed.

**Pinning is gone — placement is now sticky:**
- A module gets a slot once (on add, drop, or import) and keeps it. Cables, deletions, and edits elsewhere never move it.
- Dropping onto an occupied run displaces only the modules that run covers, to the nearest free run. Enabling options that grow a module's span does the same: it holds its slot, the covered neighbor steps aside.
- Modules with no room park past button 40 (export still blocked with the per-page message) and re-enter automatically when a deletion or move frees space.
- Imported layouts stay verbatim, including authored overlaps.

**Drag-to-place:** the inspector's 8×5 grid now takes a drag (click still works as a zero-distance drag). Every drag step re-derives displacement from a pre-drag snapshot, so a neighbor pushed aside returns the moment you drag elsewhere; release keeps what the preview shows. Grabbing one of a multi-button module's own buttons drags by that button.

**Cmd+Del bug — found and fixed.** The AppKit key monitor is installed once and its closure captured the `PatchDocument` reference. Opening a .bin swaps in a fresh document, so ⌫/⌘⌫ were deleting from the dead one: the selection binding (still live) cleared, closing the inspector, while the canvas rendered the new document where the module survived. The monitors now reinstall whenever the document identity changes. Plain ⌫ was equally broken after a file open; right-click worked because the context menu rebuilds each render.

Two things verified by reading and tests but not by hand in the running app: the drag gesture's feel (cell math mirrors the grid's 22×16/3pt layout), and the Cmd+Del fix (the mechanism is confirmed in source; I couldn't drive the GUI here). A 30-second check on your side: open a .bin, select a module, ⌘⌫ — and drag something around the inspector grid. The one-button-per-active-block span assumption from the earlier session is still marked unverified against hardware.

I tried to delete with the shortcut and it threw an index out of range error.

Right-click rarely hit it because the deleted module usually wasn't the one the inspector had open. **The crash.** My Cmd+Del fix exposed a latent bug rather than introducing one: the inspector's binding closures (name field, color/page/option pickers, param sliders) captured an array *index* into `document.modules`. **Launch restore.** The app now reopens the last successfully opened patch at startup instead of untitled. It stores a bookmark (not a path, so it survives the file being moved) on every successful open — importer, Finder drop, and double-click all funnel through the same function. If the file no longer exists, the bookmark is cleared quietly and you get untitled; a corrupt file still surfaces the normal error alert.

# ZOIA Canvas

Design [Empress Effects ZOIA](https://empresseffects.com/products/zoia) patches
on your Mac — a full-screen node canvas instead of one button at a time on the
pedal. Open real `.bin` patch files, rewire and tweak them, hear them play, and
save files the pedal loads straight from its SD card.

![The canvas with a patch open](docs/canvas.png)

## Features

- **Node canvas** — every module is a node, every connection is a cable you can
  see. Pages appear as side-by-side framed bands, with an LED-grid preview of
  each page in the bar along the bottom.
- **Live playback** — press Play and hear the patch through a built-in audio
  engine. Signal animates through the canvas: audio wires draw the waveform
  they carry, CV cables pulse as gates travel, cables blush red/blue as values
  rise and fall, and modules glow with their output.
- **Full editing** — add modules from the searchable palette, wire by dragging
  between ports, set every option and parameter in the inspector, name and
  color modules, organize pages.
- **Pedal-true layout** — the inspector shows each page as the 8×5 button grid
  the pedal will display, and you drag modules to the buttons you want.
  Placement is sticky: nothing moves unless you move it or something you moved
  displaces it.
- **Real patch files** — the `.bin` format is byte-verified against the entire
  ZOIA and Euroburo factory patch libraries. What you save is what the pedal
  reads.

![Playback: waveforms travel the wires](docs/playing.png)

## Installing

Build from source (requires Xcode and [xcodegen](https://github.com/yonaskolb/XcodeGen)):

```
xcodegen
xcodebuild -scheme ZoiaCanvas build
```

The app lands in Xcode's DerivedData products folder; drag `ZoiaCanvas.app`
wherever you like.

## Opening patches

Any of:

- **⌘O** or the folder button in the toolbar
- Drag a `.bin` anywhere onto the window
- Double-click a `.bin` in Finder (ZOIA Canvas registers as an editor)

On launch the app reopens whatever you had open last. Patches straight off the
pedal's SD card open as-is, and imported layouts arrange themselves
circuit-style — signal flowing left to right.

## Working the canvas

| Action | How |
| --- | --- |
| Pan | two-finger scroll, or drag empty canvas |
| Zoom | pinch, or ⌘+ / ⌘− / ⌘0 to reset |
| Add a module | drag it from the palette, or click it to drop one in |
| Move a module | drag its body |
| Select | click a module or cable |
| Delete | ⌫ or ⌘⌫ on the selection, or right-click a module |
| Wire | drag from an output port to an input port |
| Re-route a wire | drag it off the input port it's plugged into, drop it on another — drop on empty space to disconnect |
| Jump between pages | click a page tile in the bottom bar |

Audio ports are blue, CV ports orange. The app enforces output→input
direction and warns (without blocking) when you cross audio and CV — the pedal
allows it, so the canvas does too. Cable style (curved or angular) is a toolbar
toggle, as is the expanded layout that gives every cross-page connection its
own connector card.

## The inspector

Click a module and the right panel shows everything about it:

- **Name and color** — what the pedal displays and the LED color it lights.
- **Grid** — the module's page as the pedal's 8×5 button grid. Drag the module
  to the buttons you want; whatever you drop on steps aside and comes back if
  you keep dragging. A page over its 40 buttons shows a warning and blocks
  saving until it fits.
- **Options** — every catalog option; changing one re-lays-out the module's
  blocks live, exactly as the pedal does.
- **Params** — a slider per parameter, readable as raw CV or as the MIDI note
  the pitch mapping lands on.

## Playing patches

Press **Play** in the toolbar. The engine renders the patch in real time
through your output device; the **Input** menu picks what feeds the patch's
audio-input modules — the microphone, or a loopback device like BlackHole to
route another app in. The DSP meter estimates load the way the pedal's own
meter does.

A growing subset of the module catalog is implemented in the engine;
unimplemented modules pass silence. Pitch and LFO response curves are
documented approximations pending calibration against hardware — trust the
pedal's ears over the preview.

## Saving

- **⌘S** saves back to the open file. The title shows `*` while there are
  unsaved changes; an untitled patch asks where to live the first time.
- **⌘E** exports a copy without touching the open file.

Copy the saved `.bin` to the pedal's SD card and load it like any other patch.

## Keyboard shortcuts

| | |
| --- | --- |
| ⌘O | open |
| ⌘S | save |
| ⌘E | export a copy |
| ⌫ / ⌘⌫ | delete selection |
| ⌘+ / ⌘− / ⌘0 | zoom in / out / reset |

## For developers

The project is SwiftUI, generated by `xcodegen` from `project.yml`, with a
test suite covering the codec (oracle-tested against
[zoia_lib](https://github.com/meanmedianmoge/zoia_lib)'s parser over the full
factory corpus), the block-layout engine, grid placement, and the audio
runtime. `xcodebuild -scheme ZoiaCanvas test` runs everything. The patch
binary format and module metadata derive from zoia_lib (GPL-3.0) and
Empress's firmware-5 module index.

## License

GPL-3.0 — see LICENSE.
